summary: A one-line correction to RFC 107. On page 7 of that document a command shown as RTS should have been STR. Short errata notes like this were issued as RFCs in the early days.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 124 corrects one item on page 7 of RFC 107. It says to read RTS as STR.

questions: what correction was made on page 7 of rfc 107
what should replace rts on page 7 of rfc 107
subtitle: A one-sentence correction to RFC 107.

tldr.problem: A command on page 7 of RFC 107 was printed incorrectly.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 124 states that the item shown as RTS should be STR.
tldr.outcome: RFC 124 updates RFC 107 with this correction.

today: RFC 124 updates RFC 107 with this typographical correction. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces RFC 124.

sections.title: The Corrected Command
sections.content: The entire correction is one sentence: on page 7 of RFC 107, RTS (1.) should be an STR.
sections.plainLanguage: On page 7 of RFC 107, read STR where the text shows RTS.

sections.title: An Erratum Issued as an RFC
sections.content: RFC 124 is a short correction note dated 19 April 1971. The text does not define the meanings of RTS or STR; it only identifies the correction.
sections.plainLanguage: The note corrects a command name and does not explain the commands themselves.

sections.title: What Changes in RFC 107
sections.content: Readers of RFC 107 should apply this correction to the command shown on page 7. RFC 124 supplies no other protocol changes.
sections.plainLanguage: The correction applies only to the command on page 7 of RFC 107.
